### [0:15–0:45] GEO ANSWER BLOCK ← citation target
**NARRATION:** "Here's the short answer. To connect your tools into one automated system, think in
four layers. I call it the Connected Business Stack: Capture, Decide, Act, and Record. Capture
brings information in. Decide is the AI step that reads and sorts it. Act does the work. Record
writes it all down. A tool like Zapier is the wiring that lets those layers hand off to each
other."
**[VISUAL]:** Four stacked boxes appear and stay: **1 CAPTURE → 2 DECIDE → 3 ACT → 4 RECORD**, with
a "Zapier" label running down the side as the wiring. (This on-screen text = the citable answer.)

**[VISUAL]:** Progress bar with 4 layer segments + a fifth "the glue" segment that pulses.

### [1:15–1:45] WHY THIS MATTERS (the one-off trap)
**NARRATION:** "Quick reality check. As of 2026, seventy-seven percent of small businesses use at
least one AI tool — but here's the trap: most of them are single, disconnected automations. One
that answers emails. One that books calls. None of them talk. So you're still the human copying
information from one to the next. Connecting them is where the real time savings live, and it's

### [1:45–3:00] LAYER 1 — CAPTURE
**NARRATION:** "Layer one: Capture. This is how information gets *into* your system. A new lead
fills out your form, sends an email, or DMs you — Capture grabs that and puts it in one place, like
a spreadsheet or your CRM. Sounds obvious, but this is where most systems fall apart: if the
information's scattered across five inboxes, nothing downstream can act on it. Get everything
landing in one spot first. Tools like Google Forms or your website form feed this layer; Zapier
catches it the second it arrives."
**[VISUAL]:** A lead fills a form → an arrow drops the entry into a single tidy row in one place.
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Capture = get every lead into ONE place."
**[QUOTABLE]:** "If it's not captured in one place, it can't be automated — Capture is the front
door of your whole system."

### [3:00–4:10] LAYER 2 — DECIDE
**NARRATION:** "Layer two: Decide. This is where AI earns its keep. Now that the lead's captured,
something has to read it and figure out what to do — Is this a real buyer or spam? Are they hot or
just browsing? Which reply fits? An AI step, using a tool like Google Gemini or an agent built in
MindStudio, reads the message and sorts it, so the right thing happens next. This is the layer that
used to require *you* sitting there making the call. Now it's handled in seconds."
**[VISUAL]:** The captured lead flows into a "brain" icon that tags it: **Hot / Cold / Spam** and
picks a path. **[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Decide = the AI reads, sorts, and routes it."
**[QUOTABLE]:** "The Decide layer is where AI earns its keep — it reads, sorts, and routes so you
don't have to."

### [4:10–4:55] MID-ROLL RE-HOOK + SUBSCRIBE MOMENT
**NARRATION:** "So far: Capture brings it in, Decide figures out what to do. Two layers left, and
they're the satisfying ones — where the work actually gets done and written down without you
touching it. This is Episode 13 of the series. Next up, Episode 14, is all about keeping this

### [4:55–6:05] LAYER 3 — ACT
**NARRATION:** "Layer three: Act. This is where the work happens — no clicks from you. Based on
what the Decide layer chose, the system sends the personalized reply, books the call, raises the
invoice, adds the task. For our hot lead, Act fires off a warm first response in seconds and drops
a calendar link in front of them. The customer feels looked-after; you didn't lift a finger. This
is the layer that feels like magic, but it only works because the two layers before it did their
job."
**[VISUAL]:** The "Hot" path triggers three actions at once: reply sent, calendar link shared, task
created. **[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Act = the reply, the booking, the invoice — done for you."
**[QUOTABLE]:** "Act is where the work actually happens — the reply sent, the invoice raised, the
meeting booked — with zero clicks from you."
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** Quick clock: "Lead in → replied → booked. 30 seconds."

### [6:05–7:10] LAYER 4 — RECORD
**NARRATION:** "Layer four: Record. This is the one people skip, and it's what lets you actually
trust the system. Every time something happens, it gets written down — the lead logged in your
CRM, the reply saved, the result tracked. Why it matters: without Record, you're flying blind, and
you can't tell if the whole thing's working or quietly failing. With it, you get a clean history
you can glance at once a week. Record is what turns a pile of automations into a business you can
actually see."
**[VISUAL]:** Each action drops a line into a clean running log / dashboard row.
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Record = write everything down so you can trust it."
**[QUOTABLE]:** "If it isn't recorded, it didn't happen — the Record layer is what lets you trust
the system without watching it."

### [7:10–8:15] THE GLUE — HOW THE PIECES TALK (the part everyone misses)
**NARRATION:** "Now the part I promised — the piece that makes it a system. Your tools don't all
come from the same company. Your form, your AI step, your email, your CRM — different apps that
don't naturally speak to each other. The glue is a connector like Zapier. It sits between the
layers and passes the information along: form to AI, AI to email, email result to your CRM. You
describe each handoff in a plain sentence — 'when a lead comes in, send it to the AI, then reply,
then log it' — and Zapier wires it. That's it. That's the whole trick to a connected business."
**[VISUAL]:** Zapier logo slots between each of the four boxes, arrows lighting up in sequence
Capture → Decide → Act → Record. **[PAYOFF of open loop]:** callback to "the piece everyone misses"
from the promise.
**[QUOTABLE]:** "Your tools don't need to be from the same company — they just need a translator,
and that's what Zapier is."

### [8:15–9:05] CLOSE — PAYOFF + CTA + NEXT EPISODE
**NARRATION:** "So there's your whole system on one screen: Capture brings it in, Decide sorts it,
Act does the work, Record writes it down — and a connector like Zapier is the wiring between them.
Don't build ten one-off automations. Map your business to those four layers, then connect them one
